headline: SILVER SPIKES 7% TO $44.44 — Gold/Silver Ratio Falls to 82.5 as Metals Rally Broadens; Gold Rises to $3,631
snippet: Spot silver surged 6.9–10.4% on November 27, reaching an intraday high of $44.44 per troy ounce — the strongest single-session advance in weeks — as the gold/silver ratio fell from 85.87 on Thursday to approximately 82.53. Gold also climbed roughly 1.3% to $3,631 as the metals complex broadly recovered from recent multi-month lows. The move arrived on a Friday thinned by holiday-week trade and arrived as buyers stepped in after both metals breached one-year support levels earlier in the week.

headline: COPPER BIGGEST GAIN IN 10 MONTHS — LME Up 6.5% to $12,600 as AI Jitters Clear and China Policy Support Returns
snippet: LME copper surged as much as 6.5% to above $12,600 per tonne on November 27 — its largest single-day gain since late January — as risk appetite returned following a week dominated by AI-sector anxiety. Shanghai copper futures jumped 5.22%, marking their strongest advance since January. Short covering added momentum, and the move put copper on track for its first positive week since early October, though the metal remains well below its September record near $15,000/t.

headline: GENESIS VAULTS TO AUSTRALIA'S #3 GOLD PRODUCER — $12.6B Merger With Vault Closes; 600,000+ Oz/yr Combined
snippet: Genesis Minerals has completed its landmark acquisition of Vault Minerals in a deal the two companies valued at approximately A$12.6 billion, creating a combined entity the CEO described as Australia's 'perfect pairing' and the country's third-largest listed gold producer. The merged company is projected to produce 600,000 to 700,000 ounces of gold annually, with CEO Raleigh Finlayson flagging possible non-core mine sales to focus capital on the highest-quality Western Australian assets.

headline: GOLD JUNIORS AT 0.51X NAV: VALUE TRAP OR GENERATIONAL ENTRY? Analyst Models Still Price Gold at $2,300/oz
snippet: An analysis of gold mining valuations finds mid-cap and junior miners trading at approximately 0.51x price-to-NAV — their cheapest level in years relative to gold prices — while technology stocks trade above 22x EV/EBITDA. The report attributes the discount partly to analyst models that still use a long-term gold price near $2,300/oz, creating structural undervaluation of mine earnings at current $3,600+ gold. The key question for investors: does the discount reflect genuine risk (debt, costs, jurisdiction) or stale assumptions?

headline: URNM DOWN 31% WHILE URANIUM HOLDS $90 — 'The Disconnect Is Historic': Why Miners Aren't Tracking the Metal
snippet: An analysis breaks down the growing gap between uranium spot prices (near $90/lb, up 10% year-over-year) and uranium equity performance (URNM down 31% over the same period). The divergence is attributed to Cameco's Q3 2026 earnings disappointment, rising production costs consuming margin that rising spot prices should theoretically deliver, and institutional rotation away from non-yielding assets — the same headwind crushing gold equities.

headline: CHINA RARE EARTH MAGNET EXPORTS +4% YOY IN OCTOBER — SMM Projects 13% Full-Year Growth as EV Demand Holds Firm
snippet: October 2026 data confirmed a 4% year-over-year increase in China's permanent magnet exports — the processed rare earth products used in EV motors and wind turbines — with Shanghai Metals Market projecting full-year growth of approximately 13% versus 2025. The data contrasts with ongoing weakness in raw rare earth oxide prices, suggesting that value-added processing rather than primary mining is capturing the bulk of demand growth. Praseodymium-neodymium alloy prices held steady while raw oxides softened.

headline: JUNIOR MINERS DEFYING 2026 BEAR MARKET — Several ASX Developers Up 50%+ as Sector Bleeds
snippet: An analysis of ASX-listed junior miners in the second half of 2026 finds a cluster of development-stage companies that have bucked the broader sector selloff, posting gains of 50% or more even as GDXJ dropped 16.5% year-to-date through October. Common threads among the outperformers include resource upgrades, significant high-grade drill results near existing deposits, and low-capex development paths that remain financeable without debt — a useful checklist for retail investors hunting value in a downturn.

headline: JUNIOR MINING CONSOLIDATION ACCELERATES — M&A Wave Builds at Decade-Low Developer Valuations
snippet: With junior gold and base metal developers trading at the steepest discounts to NAV in roughly a decade, the November 2026 wave of M&A deals — from the $12.6 billion Genesis/Vault combination to smaller TSXV deals — reflects strategic acquisition by well-capitalised buyers rather than a broad return of risk appetite. The analysis argues retail investors should distinguish between companies being acquired for genuine asset value versus those desperate to merge to survive cash burn.

headline: NdPr RISES, LITHIUM SOFTENS, COBALT HOLDS — SP Angel Nov 27 Metals Brief Shows Battery Complex Diverging
snippet: SP Angel's November 27 morning metals brief flags a divergence within the battery metals complex: neodymium-praseodymium alloy prices continued to strengthen alongside cobalt's DRC-ban driven rally, while lithium carbonate continued to soften even as copper staged its largest intraday rally in 10 months. The brief highlights that not all battery metals are moving together — a critical distinction for investors deciding which part of the supply chain to weight.

headline: MINING STOCKS LIFT FTSE TO BEST WEEK IN 8 MONTHS — Global Equity Recovery Starting to Raise All Miner Boats
snippet: UK mining stocks led the FTSE 100 to its best weekly gain in eight months on November 27, as a broadening global equity recovery lifted shares across the sector. Rio Tinto, Anglo American, and Antofagasta all featured among the week's leaders, suggesting that the sharp September-to-November selloff in mining equities is beginning to attract buyers ahead of a potential year-end rebalancing. For TSX-V and ASX investors, the FTSE move reinforces Friday's signal that sentiment is stabilising.
